newsitem.title: UK: Tesco profits jump, sales still growing.
newsitem.headline: Tesco profits jump, sales still growing.

text.p: Leading British supermarket group Tesco Plc, reporting a 10.7 percent rise in first-half profits, said on Tuesday strong growth in sales had continued in the second half.

Profit before tax rose to 321 million pounds ($498.1 million) from 290 million last year, and chairman Sir Ian MacLaurin said that despite falling food price inflation and marketing moves by competitors: "In the opening five weeks of our second half...our sales in the UK have continued to move strongly ahead."
Tesco profits jump, sales still growing

The profit figure excludes gains on disposals and came on a 14 percent rise in gross sales to 6.72 billion pounds. But operating profit in Britain rose by just 6.5 percent, as Tesco said a price war between petrol retailers coupled with higher oil prices "significantly affected" petrol profits and overall UK operating margins.

MacLaurin said in the results statement that sales from comparable stores were currently running 7.5 percent ahead of last year, giving underlying growth of four percent after allowing for price inflation of 3.5 percent.

He said the British market remained very competitive but said Tesco, which has overtaken J. Sainsbury Plc in terms of market share -- which it put at 14 percent in the first half -- would continue to develop its business and believed it would be able to maintain its momentum.
Tesco said its sales growth in Britain continued to outperform the industry average. It raised its dividend by 6.6 percent to 3.25 pence. ($1=.6444 Pound)
